t: This is Thurloe Street, in Kensington and Chelsea. It carries the name of John Thurloe, an English barrister from Great Milton in Oxfordshire. During the Protectorate he was secretary to the council of state, and he was spymaster for Oliver Cromwell. He also held the office of Postmaster General from 1655 to 1660, so the man behind this street name was at the centre of Cromwell's government.
